findings.description: The old code loaded each distinct sensor's calibration once per batch. The new `calibrated()` calls `source.load()` for every reading, so a batch with N readings runs N SQL queries instead of one per sensor. Large batches become slow and put needless load on the database.
findings.suggestion: Cache calibrations per sensor_id within `summarize` (a dict, or a local memo passed into `calibrated`) so each sensor is loaded once per batch.
findings.title: Calibration loaded from the database for every reading

findings.description: A zone is marked 'inspect' when `mean is None` or the rejected share is too high. The reason always says '{rejected} readings out of range'. With a policy where `max_rejected_share` is below the actual share the message is accurate, but a zone with `mean is None` and `rejected == 0` cannot occur from `summarize`. For other callers building summaries by hand, the message would read '0 readings out of range', which hides the real cause.
findings.suggestion: Build the reason from the actual condition, for example 'no valid readings' versus 'X of Y readings rejected'.
findings.title: Inspect reason is misleading when there are no rejected readings
